item.title: Company's safety record raises questions after massive L.A. warehouse fire
item.description: The massive food warehouse fire in Los Angeles in June followed a long run of fires at properties tied to one of the world's largest cold storage companies, a CBS News investigation has found.

item.title: Logistics company involved in Los Angeles warehouse fire linked to many similar incidents
item.description: Matt Gutman investigates Lineage Logistics, the company involved in the Los Angeles warehouse fire that left tens of millions of pounds of meat to rot, forcing a whole community to face foul odors and other health hazards.

item.title: Sen. Bernie Sanders calls El-Sayed's Michigan primary win "unprecedented in modern American history"
item.description: Independent Sen. Bernie Sanders of Vermont on Wednesday lauded Abdul El-Sayed for his victory in the Michigan Democratic Senate primary, calling it "literally unprecedented in modern American history." Associated Press politics reporter Matt Brown and NOTUS Senate reporter Igor Bobic join "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: At least 17 killed in Ukraine after Russian strikes on capital of Kyiv and surrounding region
item.description: At least 17 people have been killed by new Russian strikes on Ukraine as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy highlights the need for more interceptor missiles. Holly Williams has more.

item.title: Latest on Trump's support for Max Miller's reelection campaign amid abuse allegations
item.description: Republican Rep. Max Miller of Ohio is defying pressure from both parties to end his reelection campaign amid domestic abuse allegations, which he denies. Axios White House reporter Marc Caputo joins "The Takeout" with the latest on President Trump's response.

item.title: Progressive Abdul El-Sayed projected to win Michigan Democratic Senate primary
item.description: Former state health official Abdul El-Sayed faced Rep. Haley Stevens in the Democratic Senate primary in Michigan in a closely watched contest that represented the latest test of the party's divisions.

item.title: What the deportation of over 300,000 Haitians could mean for U.S. healthcare, hospitality
item.description: As temporary protected status benefits are lifted for over 300,000 Haitians, the U.S. could feel the impact across the nursing industry, at hotels, and more. Cristian Benavides reports.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed to face Republican Mike Rogers after Michigan Senate primary win
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed is the Democratic nominee for Senate in Michigan after his win in Tuesday night's primary. Ed O'Keefe breaks down what his general election race against Republican Mike Rogers could look like.

item.title: At least 12 states report cyberattacks on water systems possibly linked to Iran
item.description: Cyberattacks on U.S. water systems that officials suspect may be linked to Iran-backed hackers have been reported in at least a dozen states, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: How democratic socialism is shifting politics in Washington
item.description: Democratic socialist candidates are gaining traction in races across the country, with lawmakers on both sides of the aisle appearing weary of its growing popularity. David Sirota, founder and editor-in-chief of The Lever, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Qdoba removes jalapeños as salmonella outbreak spreads to 27 states
item.description: At least 345 people — the majority in Colorado and Minnesota — have been sickened by a salmonella outbreak, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

item.title: Possible Iranian cyberattacks on water facilities spark safety fears
item.description: Cyberattacks on water and wastewater facilities in at least 12 states that are possibly linked to Iran are causing concerns about the safety of drinking water. Nicole Sganga has more.

item.title: New details on the man arrested near Trump's California golf club
item.description: A man arrested outside President Trump's golf club in Rancho Palos Verdes, California, was already under investigation for robbery. Nikole Killion has the details.

item.title: Federal investigation launched into air traffic incident involving Trump's helicopter
item.description: On Wednesday, a federal investigation was launched into an air traffic control incident involving President Trump's helicopter, Marine One. Nancy Cordes has more.

item.title: AI models are behaving unexpectedly. Experts warn of a "bumpy road" ahead.
item.description: AI models are engaging in unauthorized actions — in the most recent case, creating fake identities and attempting to persuade real people to approve malicious code.

item.title: Trump says Strait of Hormuz deal could happen as soon as today amid talks
item.description: President Trump told reporters Tuesday evening that an announcement on the Strait of Hormuz could happen today or tomorrow, following talks between Iran and Oman.

item.title: Trump comments on Democratic primaries, Iran in remarks to supporters
item.description: President Trump addressed supporters in Las Vegas on Wednesday, touching on the Iran war and the performance of Democrats in recent primary elections. CBS News' Nikole Killion reports.

item.title: SpaceX rocket booster slams into moon, creating crater that could be 16 feet deep
item.description: The impact wasn't visible to the naked eye, but photos are expected to come from a lunar satellite at a later time.

item.title: What to know after progressive Abdul El-Sayed wins Democratic Senate primary in Michigan
item.description: Progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed narrowly won his Democratic primary for Senate Tuesday night in Michigan, beating Haley Stevens by a single percentage point. CBS News' Ed O'Keefe and Anthony Salvanto has more.

item.title: Jewish Insider editor-in-chief says DSA's weaknesses go "beyond antisemitism"
item.description: The relationship between progressive candidates and Jewish voters has been a central focus this election cycle. Jewish Insider Editor in-Chief Josh Kraushaar joins "The Takeout" to discuss his new piece titled: "DSA's Achilles' Heel Goes Beyond Antisemitism."

item.title: New Mexico attorney general explains why he's suing DOJ over Epstein files
item.description: New Mexico is suing the Trump administration for access to files related to Jeffrey Epstein as it investigates the convicted sex offender's Zorro Ranch property. New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Clancy family nanny testifies that Lindsay was "a wonderful mom"
item.description: The last nanny who worked for the Clancy family testified at trial that Lindsay was a wonderful mom who loved her children.

item.title: FAA probing Marine One safety incident around National Airport
item.description: When the helicopter that transports President Trump crosses the Potomac, Reagan Washington National Airport is required to impose a ground stop on air traffic.

item.title: Some Gen Zers swap smartphones for "dumb" phones in a bid to unplug
item.description: "It really opens up your mind," said one 23-year-old who ditched smartphones to wean herself off social media.

item.title: Popular influencer shot dead during livestream outside restaurant
item.description: Cesar Gastelum, who had more than 600,000 followers on TikTok, was broadcasting with two friends when he was killed.

item.title: Perez Hilton hospitalized after livestreaming acts of self-harm, officials say
item.description: In the livestream, which has since been taken down, Hilton appears to be bloodied and in a distressed mental state.

item.title: Disney partners with TikTok to offer creator content on its app
item.description: Disney and TikTok are teaming up to let users create short-form videos that draw on the entertainment giant's large stable of movies and TV shows.

item.title: White House declassifies info on secret FBI probe into Trump's firing of Comey
item.description: The White House has declassified information claiming the FBI probed whether President Trump acted as a Russian asset when he fired James Comey, a theory an administration official said wasn't backed up by evidence.

item.title: Nazi warships, mammoth bones emerge as Danube River dries up
item.description: Water levels on the Danube River have dropped so low that dozens of World War II German battleships – and even the remains of an ancient woolly mammoth — are emerging into view.

item.title: Cyclospora outbreak dubbed "lettuce-gate" as health concerns spread across U.S.
item.description: Americans say they aren't convinced the cyclospora outbreak is under control as confirmed cases near 2,000.
